newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - GrandMet sell-off attracts offers.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - GrandMet sell-off attracts offers.

text.p: Food and drink company Grand Metropolitan has already received interest from prospective buyers for its national European food businesses and expects to complete the sell-off by January 1997.

"We have received good robust interest...We have people indicating strong interest and indicating prices that are acceptable to us," said Paul Walsh, chief executive of GrandMet's The Pillsbury Company.
Earlier GrandMet said it will consider selling its remaining national food businesses in the UK and Continental Europe.

These are Shippams, Peter's Savoury Products, Memory Lane Cakes and Fleur de Lys in Britain, Hofmann-Menu and Goldstein in Germany, Brossard in France and Italy, Suzy and Desobry in Belgium and Driehoek in the Netherlands.

Their combined sales last year were 370 million stg with operating profit of 10 million and operating capital used of 129 million stg at September 30, 1995. This does not include written-off goodwill of 207 million stg.
Analysts estimate the sell-off would fetch about 140 million stg.

GrandMet's European foods business posted a trading profit of 23 million stg in the year to September 1995, up from 12 million stg in 1994, after a hefty restructuring and plant closure programme undertaken in 1993.

The company does not disclose earnings for subsidiaries, but Brossard is easily the largest and similar in sales terms to Germany's Erasco Group which Campbell Soup agreed today to buy from GrandMet for about $210 million.
Before the announcement GrandMet's European Foods business showed sales of $1.2 billion which is forecast to fall to about $450 million once the sales are complete.
"My plan in foods is to focus on our leading brands," said Walsh, adding that the sell-off of so-called tertiary brands will allow GrandMet to concentrate on its main brands.
The businesses were also providing an inadequate return on capital, said Walsh.
"You can expect GrandMet to be very eager to improve total return to shareholders. Several of us have held this view for a long while."
"I think its compatible with GrandMet's mission to improve shareholder returns. We intend to fix that."
